objects.description: An alias type representing an atomic or volatile boolean depending on C++ standard availability. Under C++20 or later it is std::atomic<bool>; otherwise it degrades to volatile bool.

An alias type representing an atomic or volatile 32-bit unsigned integer depending on C++ standard availability. Under C++20 or later it is std::atomic<uint32_t>; otherwise it degrades to volatile uint32_t.

objects.definition: typedef volatile uint16_t atomic_uint16_t;
objects.description: A typedef alias for a volatile 16-bit unsigned integer. Used where atomic-like semantics are desired without C++ std::atomic.

objects.definition: typedef volatile const uint16_t atomic_const_uint16_t;
objects.description: A typedef alias for a volatile const 16-bit unsigned integer. Intended for read-only values that may change outside normal program flow (e.g., ISR-updated registers).

objects.description: Enumeration of all supported IR protocols/encodings used by the library’s decoder/encoder. Values are stable and appended only at the end to maintain numbering compatibility.

A simple microsecond-resolution timer class that measures elapsed time since construction or the last reset. It accounts for a single wrap-around of the underlying system timer. Public API provides construction, resetting, and querying elapsed microseconds; in unit-test builds a static add() allows simulating passage of time. Internal state is a 32-bit start timestamp in microseconds.

A simple millisecond-resolution timer class that measures elapsed time since construction or the last reset. It accounts for a single wrap-around of the underlying system timer. Public API provides construction, resetting, and querying elapsed milliseconds; in unit-test builds a static add() allows simulating passage of time. Internal state is a 32-bit start timestamp in milliseconds.
Interrupt-handler data block for the IR receiver. Holds capture state, buffer, sizes, and timing counters used while sampling IR marks/spaces. atomic_irparams_t is a volatile alias for use in ISRs.
Small result record returned by matching/parsing helpers, indicating success, the matched data, and how many raw buffer entries were consumed.

Container for a decoded IR message. Holds the protocol type and either scalar value/address/command or a raw state byte array, plus metadata such as bit count, raw capture buffer pointer/length, overflow flag, and repeat indicator. Note: decode_type_t and atomic_uint16_t are referenced from other headers and not defined here.

IR receiver/decoder class. Manages capture, tolerance, and decoding of raw IR signals into decode_results across many protocols. Constructor configures pin, buffer size, timeout, and optional ESP32 timer number. Owns/uses an irparams_t instance for ISR state. Numerous private helpers implement protocol matching.
direct_api_constructors: IRrecv::IRrecv

Strongly-typed enum of common A/C fan speed settings used by stdAc.
Strongly-typed enum of vertical louvre (swing) positions for A/Cs.
Strongly-typed enum describing the high-level command kind an A/C remote may send.
Strongly-typed enum of horizontal louvre (swing) positions for A/Cs.
Holds a normalized set of A/C state parameters for the common A/C API. Includes mode, temperature, fan, swing, and option flags. Some fields use sentinel values when unset.
Enum of supported Fujitsu A/C remote model identifiers used to select protocol quirks.
Enum of supported Gree A/C remote model variants.
Enum for HAIER_AC176 remote configuration variants (A/B).
Enum for HITACHI_AC1 remote configuration variants (A/B).
Enum of MIRAGE A/C remote model identifiers.
Enum of Panasonic A/C remote families for protocol differences.
Enum of Sharp A/C remote model identifiers.
Enum of TCL/Teknopoint A/C remote model identifiers.
Enum of Voltas A/C remote models.
Enum of Whirlpool A/C remote models.
Enum of Kelon/Hisense (Kelon168) remote model identifiers.
Enum of LG A/C remote models and protocol variants.
Enum of Argo A/C remote model identifiers.
Enum to differentiate Toshiba generic remote variants used by the library.
IR transmitter class capable of generating many consumer IR protocols on ESP8266/ESP32. Construct with output pin and options; call begin() then various send...() helpers to transmit codes.
direct_api_constructors: IRsend::IRsend

objects.description: This header does not define any structs, enums, typedefs, or classes. It only includes other headers and sets up preprocessor macros to select a locale-specific header and then a defaults header. Any custom types would be defined in the included headers, not here.

Native 56-bit wire-format representation for Airton A/C IR messages. Provides access as a 64-bit raw value or via bitfields grouped roughly by protocol bytes, including header, mode, power, fan, turbo, temperature, swing, economy, sleep, heat, health, light, and checksum fields. Used to build/parse messages; checksum semantics are protocol-specific.

High-level controller for Airton 56-bit A/C IR protocol. Wraps IR sending, state manipulation, conversions to/from common AC abstractions, and checksum calculation/validation. Holds an AirtonProtocol instance as internal state and an IR sender (IRsend or IRsendTest under UNIT_TEST).
direct_api_constructors: IRAirtonAc::IRAirtonAc(const uint16_t pin, const bool inverted, const bool use_modulation)

objects.description: Native wire-format representation for an Airwell A/C IR message. It is a 64-bit union exposing the raw value and a bitfield view with fields: PowerToggle (1 bit), Mode (3 bits), Fan (2 bits), Temp (4 bits), plus unnamed padding. Used to pack/unpack protocol fields directly.

High-level helper for composing, converting, and transmitting Airwell A/C IR messages. Owns an IR transmitter instance (IRsend or IRsendTest) and an AirwellProtocol state. Provides setters/getters for mode, fan, temperature, and power toggle; raw accessors; conversions to/from common stdAc types; and optionally send/calibrate when SEND_AIRWELL is enabled. Construction requires an output pin and optional flags for inversion and modulation.
direct_api_constructors: IRAirwellAc::IRAirwellAc(uint16_t, bool, bool)

objects.description: Native packed representation for an Amcor A/C IR message. Provides a raw byte array of length kAmcorStateLength and an overlay of bitfields for protocol fields (Mode, Fan, Temp, Power, Max, Vent, checksum Sum). Intended to be filled and transmitted/parsed by the IRAmcorAc class.

High-level helper for constructing, validating, and transmitting Amcor A/C IR messages. Owns an AmcorProtocol state buffer and an IR sender (IRsend or IRsendTest). Provides setters/getters for power, temp, fan, mode, max, raw state access, checksum utilities, conversions to/from common AC abstractions, and optional sending/calibration when SEND_AMCOR is enabled. Construction requires an output pin and optional inversion/modulation flags.
direct_api_constructors: IRAmcorAc(const uint16_t pin, const bool inverted = false, const bool use_modulation = true)

objects.description: Native packed-bit representation of an Argo Ulisse A/C IR message for the WREM-2 remote. Provides multiple overlay views of the 12-byte state including header, payload fields, and checksum nibbles.
Native packed-bit representation of Argo WREM-3 IR messages. Union overlays cover AC control, iFeel temp report, timer, and config frames with a shared header.
Enumeration of IR message/frame types used by Argo remotes (WREM-2/3). Values match WREM-3 on-air encoding.
A/C operating modes with bit values matching WREM-3 protocol.
Fan speed settings for Argo A/Cs; values match WREM-3 protocol.
Vertical swing (flap) positions including AUTO and FULL sweep; values match WREM-3 encoding.
Timer selection for WREM-3 timer command frames: no timer, delay, or one of three schedule timers.
Day-of-week enumeration used by WREM-3 scheduling/timer functionality.

Templated base class encapsulating common Argo A/C protocol handling (state, checksum, conversions, send). Instantiated for ArgoProtocol and ArgoProtocolWREM3. Abstract by intent; constructed with IR send pin and options.
direct_api_constructors: IRArgoACBase<ArgoProtocol>(uint16_t,bool,bool)
IRArgoACBase<ArgoProtocolWREM3>(uint16_t,bool,bool)

objects.description: Concrete controller for Argo SAC-WREM2 protocol. Adds convenience methods and deprecated byte-valued setters/getters for backward compatibility.
direct_api_constructors: IRArgoAC(uint16_t,bool,bool)

objects.description: Concrete controller for Argo SAC-WREM3 protocol, exposing additional features (eco, light, filter), IR channel selection, config KV, and rich timer/schedule controls with weekday bitmaps.
direct_api_constructors: IRArgoAC_WREM3(uint16_t,bool,bool)

objects.definition:
union Bosch144Protocol {
  uint8_t raw[kBosch144StateLength];  ///< The state in IR code form.
  struct {
    uint8_t               :8;   // Fixed value 0b10110010 / 0xB2.   ############
    uint8_t InnvertS1_1   :8;   // Invert byte  0b01001101 / 0x4D   #
    uint8_t               :5;   // not used (without timer use)     #
    uint8_t FanS1         :3;   // Fan speed bits in Section 1      #
    uint8_t InnvertS1_2   :8;   // Invert byte                      # Section 1
    uint8_t               :2;   // not used (without timer use)     # =
    uint8_t ModeS1        :2;   // Operation mode bits S1           # Section 2
    uint8_t TempS1        :4;   // Desired temperature (Celsius) S2 #
    uint8_t InnvertS1_3   :8;   // Invert byte (without timer use)  ############

    uint8_t               :8;   // Fixed value 0b10110010 / 0xB2.   ############
    uint8_t InnvertS2_1   :8;   // Invert byte  0b01001101 / 0x4D   #
    uint8_t               :5;   // not used (without timer use)     #
    uint8_t FanS2         :3;   // Fan speed bits in Section 2      #
    uint8_t InnvertS2_2   :8;   // Invert byte                      # Section 2
    uint8_t               :2;   // not used (without timer use)     # =
    uint8_t ModeS2        :2;   // Operation mode bits S2           # Section 1
    uint8_t TempS2        :4;   // Desired temperature (Celsius) S2 #
    uint8_t InnvertS2_3   :8;   // Invert byte (without timer use)  ###########

    uint8_t               :8;   // Fixed value 0b11010101 / 0xD5    ###########
    uint8_t ModeS3        :1;   // ModeBit in Section 3             #
    uint8_t FanS3         :6;   // Fan speed bits in Section 3      #
    uint8_t               :1;   // Unknown                          #
    uint8_t               :5;   // Unknown                          #
    uint8_t TempS4        :1;   // Desired temp                     #
    uint8_t               :1;   // Unknown                          #
    uint8_t Quiet         :1;   // Silent-Mode                      # Section 3
    uint8_t UseFahrenheit :1;   // Fahrenheit or Celcius            #
    uint8_t               :3;   // Unknown                          #
    uint8_t TempS3        :1;   // Desired temp. Bit in Section3    #
    uint8_t               :3;   // Unknown                          #
    uint8_t               :8;   // Unknown                          #
    uint8_t ChecksumS3    :8;   // Checksum from byte 13-17         ###########
  };
};
objects.description: Packed representation of the 144-bit Bosch A/C IR message. Provides both a raw byte array and a detailed bitfield layout for the three sections of the protocol, including fan, mode, temperature bits, quiet flag, Fahrenheit/Celsius flag, and checksum. Intended to be used as the wire-state for encoding/decoding IR frames.

High-level controller for composing and transmitting Bosch 144-bit A/C IR messages. Wraps IR sending backend and exposes getters/setters for power, temperature, units, fan speed, mode, and quiet mode. Maintains protocol state in a Bosch144Protocol instance and can serialize to raw bytes, convert to/from common HVAC abstractions, and send over IR.
direct_api_constructors: IRBosch144AC::IRBosch144AC

objects.description: A packed union representing a 64-bit Carrier A/C IR message. It offers two views: a 64-bit raw field and a byte/bitfield layout for protocol fields such as checksum (Sum), operating Mode, Fan speed, temperature (Temp), vertical swing (SwingV), Power, Sleep, and On/Off timer enables and values. Intended to be used as the internal state container for the Carrier 64-bit protocol.

High-level controller for Carrier 64-bit A/C IR messages. Manages an internal CarrierProtocol state, provides getters/setters for power, mode, fan, temperature, swing, sleep, on/off timers, checksum calculation/validation, raw state access, and optional sending/calibration via IRsend/IRsendTest. begin() should be called before sending. Some conversions to/from common stdAc types are provided.
direct_api_constructors: IRCarrierAc64(const uint16_t pin, const bool inverted = false, const bool use_modulation = true)

objects.description: Tagged union representing a 24-bit Coolix A/C IR message. Provides a 32-bit raw field plus a bitfield view exposing mode, temperature, sensor temperature, fan, and Zone Follow control bits. Only 24 LSBs are meaningful; upper bits unused. Used as the internal on-wire/state format for the Coolix protocol.

High-level controller for composing, managing, and transmitting Coolix A/C IR messages. Wraps an IR sender (IRsend or IRsendTest) and maintains current and saved protocol states using CoolixProtocol. Provides APIs to set power, mode, fan, temperature (C/F ranges), swing, sleep, turbo, LED, clean, Zone Follow, and to convert to/from common AC abstractions and Coolix48 raw codes.
direct_api_constructors: IRCoolixAC(const uint16_t pin, const bool inverted = false, const bool use_modulation = true)

objects.description: Native representation of one 7-byte section of a Corona A/C IR message. Fields include two header bytes, a label, a data byte pair with their bitwise inverses used for integrity, and are intended to map directly onto the protocol's section layout.

Native representation of an entire Corona A/C IR message. The union provides three views: a raw byte buffer (size kCoronaAcStateLength, defined elsewhere), an array of protocol sections, and a bitfield struct exposing key control flags (fan, econo, swing, temp, power, mode).

High-level controller for composing, manipulating, and transmitting Corona A/C IR messages. Encapsulates an IR sender (IRsend or IRsendTest) and an internal CoronaProtocol state, with APIs to set power, mode, fan, temperature, swing, econo, and timers, plus raw access and conversion to/from common stdAc abstractions. Constructor requires an output pin and optional inverted/modulation flags. Note: SEND_CORONA_AC controls availability of send/calibrate.
direct_api_constructors: IRCoronaAc

objects.description: Native packed union representing a Daikin 280-bit A/C IR message, exposing raw state buffer and bitfields for features like power, mode, temp, timers, swing, and options. Used internally by IRDaikinESP.
Packed union for Daikin2 312-bit protocol, including raw buffer and detailed bitfields: timers, humidity, swing, sensors, lights, beeps, and power/mode controls. Used by IRDaikin2.
Packed union representing Daikin216 216-bit protocol with raw state and bitfields: power, mode, temp, fan, swing, and checksums. Used by IRDaikin216.
Packed union for Daikin160 160-bit protocol exposing raw buffer and fields for power, mode, temp, fan, swing, and checksums. Used by IRDaikin160.
Packed union for Daikin176 176-bit protocol with raw state and bitfields including IDs, mode, temp, fan, swingH, and checksums. Used by IRDaikin176.
Packed union for Daikin128 128-bit protocol including mode/fan, timers, temp, swing, sleep, power, and misc feature flags. Used by IRDaikin128.
Packed union for Daikin152 152-bit protocol with raw state and fields for power, mode, temp, fan, swingV, quiet/powerful, and option flags. Used by IRDaikin152.
Packed union for Daikin64 64-bit protocol. Holds 64-bit raw state and bitfields for mode, fan, timers, temp, swingV, sleep, power, and checksum. Used by IRDaikin64.
C++ class to construct, manipulate, and send Daikin 280-bit IR messages. Owns a DaikinESPProtocol state and an IR sender. Provides high-level A/C control APIs and checksum handling.
direct_api_constructors: IRDaikinESP(const uint16_t pin, const bool inverted = false, const bool use_modulation = true)

objects.description: C++ class for Daikin2 312-bit protocol. Manages a Daikin2Protocol state and IR sender, offering rich feature control including humidity, swing, timers, lights, beeps, sensors, and checksums.
direct_api_constructors: IRDaikin2(const uint16_t pin, const bool inverted = false, const bool use_modulation = true)

objects.description: C++ class for Daikin216 216-bit protocol. Manages Daikin216Protocol state and provides A/C controls for power, mode, temp, fan, swing, quiet/powerful, with checksum handling.
direct_api_constructors: IRDaikin216(const uint16_t pin, const bool inverted = false, const bool use_modulation = true)

objects.description: C++ class for Daikin160 160-bit protocol. Provides control interface and owns Daikin160Protocol state and IR sender with checksum support.
direct_api_constructors: IRDaikin160(const uint16_t pin, const bool inverted = false, const bool use_modulation = true)

objects.description: C++ class for Daikin176 176-bit protocol. Manages state union, supports ID handling, swingH, fan/mode/temp controls, and checksum logic.
direct_api_constructors: IRDaikin176(const uint16_t pin, const bool inverted = false, const bool use_modulation = true)

objects.description: C++ class for Daikin128 128-bit protocol. Controls features including timers, sleep, quiet/powerful, econo, and lighting toggle; holds Daikin128Protocol state and handles checksums.
direct_api_constructors: IRDaikin128(const uint16_t pin, const bool inverted = false, const bool use_modulation = true)

objects.description: C++ class for Daikin152 152-bit protocol. Exposes power/mode/temp/fan/swingV and option flags, owns Daikin152Protocol state and handles checksums.
direct_api_constructors: IRDaikin152(const uint16_t pin, const bool inverted = false, const bool use_modulation = true)

objects.description: C++ class for Daikin64 64-bit protocol. Operates on a 64-bit packed state with helper conversions, timers, sleep/quiet/turbo, and checksum utilities.
direct_api_constructors: IRDaikin64(const uint16_t pin, const bool inverted = false, const bool use_modulation = true)

objects.description: Union representing a full 64-bit Delonghi A/C IR message. It exposes the raw 64-bit value and a bitfield view for individual parameters (temperature, fan, units, power, mode, boost, sleep, on/off timers, and checksum). Used as the on-wire/native state container within this header.

Class encapsulating construction, manipulation, and transmission of Delonghi A/C IR messages. Provides setters/getters for all features, checksum helpers, conversion to common AC abstractions, and optional sending/calibration when SEND_DELONGHI_AC is enabled. Internally owns a DelonghiProtocol state, an IR sender (IRsend or IRsendTest), and saved temperature/unit fields.
direct_api_constructors: IRDelonghiAc(const uint16_t pin, const bool inverted = false, const bool use_modulation = true)

objects.description: Union representing the 56-bit EcoClim A/C IR message. Exposes the raw 64-bit value and a packed bit-field view for individual protocol fields (mode, fan, timers, temps, DIP config, etc.). Only 56 bits are meaningful; remaining bits are unused. Used as the internal state container for the EcoClim encoder/sender.

High-level helper class to create, manipulate, and send EcoClim A/C IR messages. Encapsulates an IR sender (IRsend or IRsendTest) and owns an EcoclimProtocol instance holding the current state. Provides setters/getters for power, temps, fan, mode, timers, clock, and conversions to/from common stdAc representations. Construction requires an output pin and optional inversion/modulation flags; send() is available when SEND_ECOCLIM is enabled.
direct_api_constructors: IREcoclimAc(const uint16_t pin, const bool inverted = false, const bool use_modulation = true)

objects.description: Native, packed union representing an Electra A/C IR message/state. Provides both a raw byte array of kElectraAcStateLength bytes and a bitfield struct view exposing individual fields (power, mode, fan, swing, turbo, quiet, iFeel, sensor temp/update, clean, light toggle, checksum). Used as the backing storage for IRElectraAc. Exact packing/bitfield layout is compiler-dependent; code assumes 8-bit unsigned and typical bitfield ordering for AVR/ESP. Unknown/reserved bits are unnamed.

High-level controller for building, manipulating, and sending Electra A/C IR messages. Owns an ElectraProtocol state and an IR transmitter (IRsend or IRsendTest). Provides getters/setters for power, mode, temperature, fan, swing, clean, light, turbo, quiet, iFeel, and sensor settings; raw access; checksum helpers; conversions to/from common stdAc types; and optional send/calibrate when SEND_ELECTRA_AC is defined.
direct_api_constructors: IRElectraAc::IRElectraAc(uint16_t,bool,bool)

objects.description: Union that models the 12-byte Eurom IR message/state. Provides two views: a raw byte array of length kEuromStateLength and a bitfield-structured view of individual bytes for mode/temperature, power/swing, Fahrenheit value, sleep/on-timer, off-timer, and checksum related fields. Intended for serialization to/from IR payloads; checksum semantics are documented in comments.

High-level controller for Eurom A/C IR protocol. Manages an internal EuromProtocol state, provides getters/setters for power, mode, temperature (C/F), fan, swing, sleep, and timers, checksum helpers, raw accessors, and (when enabled) IR transmission and calibration via IRsend/IRsendTest. Constructor requires an output pin and optional modulation settings.
direct_api_constructors: IREuromAc(const uint16_t pin, const bool inverted = false, const bool use_modulation = true)

objects.description: A packed union that models Fujitsu A/C IR messages. It offers two views: raw byte arrays for long/short codes and a bitfield mapping of protocol fields (e.g., Id, Cmd, Temp, Mode, timers). Used to read/build on-wire IR payloads; details like checksum and some flags are model-dependent.

Facade class to construct, manipulate, and transmit Fujitsu A/C IR messages. Wraps protocol fields (mode, temp, fan, swing, timers, power) and manages long/short frame variants, checksum, and platform IR sending. Requires IRsend/IRsendTest and model enum defined elsewhere.
direct_api_constructors: IRFujitsuAC

objects.description: Native bitfield/union representation of a Goodweather HVAC IR message. Exposes the 64-bit raw value and a packed view with named bitfields for command, power, fan, mode, temperature, swing, airflow, turbo, sleep, and light. Intended to be used as the internal state container for encoding/decoding IR frames.

High-level encoder/controller for Goodweather-compatible A/C IR messages. Wraps an IR transmitter (IRsend or IRsendTest in unit tests) and manages a GoodweatherProtocol state. Provides setters/getters for power, mode, fan, swing, temperature, sleep, turbo, light, and command, plus raw state access and conversions to/from common stdAc types. Use begin() before sending; send() transmits the current state when SEND_GOODWEATHER is enabled.
direct_api_constructors: IRGoodweatherAc

objects.description: Native packed representation of a Gree A/C IR message. It overlays a raw byte array (remote_state) and a bitfield view by protocol bytes, allowing direct manipulation of individual features (mode, fan, swing, timers, etc.). Unknown fields indicate reserved or fixed values. Size matches kGreeStateLength bytes. Endianness/bitfield packing is compiler-dependent; intended for AVR/ESP toolchains used by IRremoteESP8266.

High-level controller for composing, validating, and transmitting Gree A/C IR messages. Wraps an IR sender (IRsend or IRsendTest), maintains internal state in a GreeProtocol, and offers getters/setters plus conversions to/from a common AC abstraction (stdAc). Constructor requires an output pin and optional model/inversion/modulation flags.
direct_api_constructors: IRGreeAC::IRGreeAC(const uint16_t, const gree_ac_remote_model_t, const bool, const bool)

objects.description: Native packed representation of a Haier HSU07-HEA03 A/C IR message. Provides both a raw byte array (remote_state) and a bitfield view for fields like command, temperature, timers, fan, mode, swing, health, sleep, and checksum.

Native packed representation of a 176-bit Haier A/C IR message. Exposes fields such as model, swing (vertical/horizontal), temp, power, timers, fan speeds (Fan/Fan2), turbo/quiet, sleep, button/lock, Fahrenheit flags, and dual checksums.

Native packed representation of a 160-bit Haier A/C IR message. Includes model, temp, swing V/H, power, aux heating, timers, fan and secondary fan, turbo/quiet, sleep, clean/light flags, Fahrenheit options, button/lock, and dual checksums.

High-level encoder/manager for Haier HSU07-HEA03 protocol messages. Owns an IR transmitter and a HaierProtocol state, offers getters/setters for fields, raw access, checksum validation, and send/begin/calibrate routines.

functions.description: Constructs an IRtimer that measures elapsed time in microseconds since construction or the most recent reset(). Intended for timing intervals; implementation notes indicate it compensates for a single wrap-around of the underlying system timer.
requirements: Object must be constructed before calling member functions like reset() or elapsed().
Timing accuracy and availability depend on the underlying system timer (not defined here).
Only one underlying timer wrap-around is handled; behavior after more than one wrap-around interval since the last start/reset is unspecified.

functions.name: IRtimer::reset
functions.description: Resets the IRtimer start point to the current time so that subsequent elapsed() returns the microseconds since this call. Use to restart interval measurements.
requirements: Must be called on a valid, constructed IRtimer instance.
Only one underlying system timer wrap-around interval after the reset is handled; behavior with longer runtimes without another reset is unspecified.

functions.name: IRtimer::elapsed
functions.description: Returns the number of microseconds elapsed since the IRtimer was constructed or last reset(). The class notes that it compensates for a single wrap-around of the system timer.
requirements: Must be called on a valid, constructed IRtimer instance (optionally after reset()).
Return value is a 32-bit unsigned count of microseconds; callers should handle potential wrap or overflow semantics appropriately.
Only one underlying system timer wrap-around interval since the last start/reset is handled; behavior after that is unspecified.

Only one underlying system timer wrap-around interval since the last start/reset is handled; behavior after that is unspecified.

functions.name: IRrecv::IRrecv
functions.signature: IRrecv::IRrecv(const uint16_t recvpin, const uint16_t bufsize = kRawBuf, const uint8_t timeout = kTimeoutMs, const bool save_buffer = false)
functions.description: Constructor (non-ESP32): create an IR receiver bound to a given input pin, with a raw capture buffer of size bufsize, a capture timeout (in milliseconds), and an option to retain the last captured buffer for later inspection/decoding. Typically called once during setup before enabling the receiver.
requirements: recvpin is a valid GPIO pin configured for input suitable for an IR demodulator output.
bufsize specifies the maximum number of raw intervals the receiver can store; it must be a finite, non-zero number representable by uint16_t.
timeout is in milliseconds; type-constrained to 0..255 (uint8_t).
save_buffer controls whether the raw buffer is retained; memory use increases when true.

functions.name: IRrecv::~IRrecv
functions.description: Destructor: releases any resources associated with the IR receiver instance (e.g., buffers, timers/interrupts). Normally not called explicitly in Arduino sketches.
requirements: The instance must not be used after destruction.
If interrupts/timers were enabled, they should be assumed stopped by destruction.

functions.name: IRrecv::setTolerance
functions.description: Set the default match tolerance used when comparing measured IR pulse/space durations against protocol timings. The tolerance is a percentage applied in subsequent matching operations.
requirements: percent is expressed as a percentage value (0–100 typical). Values beyond valid percentage range may be rejected or adjusted internally (exact behavior not specified).
Call before matching/decoding if a non-default tolerance is desired.

functions.name: IRrecv::getTolerance
functions.description: Get the current default tolerance percentage used for timing matches.
requirements: None beyond having a valid IRrecv instance.

functions.name: IRrecv::decode
functions.signature: bool IRrecv::decode(decode_results *results, irparams_t *save = NULL, uint8_t max_skip = 0, uint16_t noise_floor = 0)
functions.description: Attempt to decode the most recently captured IR signal into a structured result. On success, fills the provided results structure with protocol, data/state, bit length, and flags (e.g., repeat). Optional save allows copying raw capture state; max_skip/noise_floor can influence pre-filtering and matching.
requirements: results must be a valid, non-null pointer to a decode_results structure writable by the function.
If save is non-null, it must point to a valid irparams_t structure to receive a copy of the capture state.
Function should be called when new capture data is available (typically after enabling and running the receiver).
max_skip and noise_floor are optional tuning parameters; valid ranges are those of their types (uint8_t/uint16_t).

functions.name: IRrecv::enableIRIn
functions.description: Enable the IR receiver hardware/interrupts so it begins capturing raw IR signal timings on the configured pin. Optionally enables an internal pull-up on the input pin.
requirements: Must be called before attempting to capture/parse IR signals.
If pullup is true, the chosen pin should support an internal pull-up resistor; otherwise, ensure appropriate external pull-up as required by the IR demodulator.

functions.name: IRrecv::disableIRIn
functions.description: Disable the IR receiver hardware/interrupts, stopping capture of IR timings.
requirements: Do not call decode while disabled, as no new data will be captured.

functions.name: IRrecv::pause
functions.description: Temporarily pause capturing IR signal timings without tearing down the receiver configuration.
requirements: Intended to be used after enableIRIn; no capture occurs while paused.

functions.name: IRrecv::resume
functions.description: Resume capturing IR signal timings after a pause.
requirements: Call after pause to continue capturing. The receiver must have been previously enabled.

functions.name: IRrecv::getBufSize
functions.description: Return the maximum number of raw timing entries that can be stored in the capture buffer for this instance.
requirements: None beyond having a valid IRrecv instance.

functions.name: IRrecv::setUnknownThreshold
functions.description: Set the minimum raw message length needed before reporting an UNKNOWN decode. Only available when DECODE_HASH is enabled. Used to filter out very short/noisy captures from being considered as unknown protocol frames.
requirements: DECODE_HASH must be enabled at compile time for this function to be available.
length is the minimum number of raw entries; it must be a non-zero, positive value representable by uint16_t.

functions.name: IRrecv::match
functions.signature: bool IRrecv::match(const uint32_t measured, const uint32_t desired, const uint8_t tolerance = kUseDefTol, const uint16_t delta = 0)
functions.description: Generic timing comparator: returns true if a measured duration matches a desired duration within the specified tolerance and optional absolute delta. Used by decoders to verify mark/space widths.
requirements: measured and desired are timing values in the same units expected by IRrecv internals (implementation uses capture ticks).
tolerance is a percentage (or kUseDefTol to use the receiver's default).
delta is an additional absolute allowance in the same time units as measured/desired.

functions.name: IRrecv::matchMark
functions.signature: bool IRrecv::matchMark(const uint32_t measured, const uint32_t desired, const uint8_t tolerance = kUseDefTol, const int16_t excess = kMarkExcess)
functions.description: Timing comparator specialized for mark (IR carrier present) durations. Accounts for typical sensor-induced mark/space bias via the excess parameter.
requirements: measured and desired are timing values in the same internal units.
tolerance is a percentage (or kUseDefTol).
excess compensates for systematic mark measurement bias; units align with measured/desired.

functions.name: IRrecv::matchMarkRange
functions.signature: bool IRrecv::matchMarkRange(const uint32_t measured, const uint32_t desired, const uint16_t range = 100, const int16_t excess = kMarkExcess)
functions.description: Check if a mark duration falls within a range around a desired value, applying a fixed range window rather than percentage tolerance. Includes mark/space bias compensation via excess.
requirements: measured and desired are timing values in the same internal units.
range defines the allowable window around desired (units align with measured/desired).
excess compensates for systematic mark measurement bias.

functions.name: IRrecv::matchSpace
functions.signature: bool IRrecv::matchSpace(const uint32_t measured, const uint32_t desired, const uint8_t tolerance = kUseDefTol, const int16_t excess = kMarkExcess)
functions.description: Timing comparator specialized for space (no carrier) durations. Accounts for typical sensor-induced mark/space bias via the excess parameter.
requirements: measured and desired are timing values in the same internal units.
tolerance is a percentage (or kUseDefTol).
excess compensates for systematic sensor bias; units align with measured/desired.

functions.name: IRrecv::matchSpaceRange
functions.signature: bool IRrecv::matchSpaceRange(const uint32_t measured, const uint32_t desired, const uint16_t range = 100, const int16_t excess = kMarkExcess)
functions.description: Check if a space duration falls within a fixed allowable range around a desired value, including compensation for sensor bias via the excess parameter.
requirements: measured and desired are timing values in the same internal units.
range defines the allowable window around desired (units align with measured/desired).
excess compensates for systematic sensor bias.

functions.name: IRsend::IRsend
functions.signature: IRsend::IRsend(uint16_t IRsendPin, bool inverted = false, bool use_modulation = true)
functions.description: Constructor for an IR transmitter. Initializes an IRsend object for a given GPIO pin, with optional inverted output and optional carrier modulation capability.
requirements: IRsendPin must refer to a valid, output-capable GPIO pin on the target MCU.
If inverted is true, attached IR driver circuitry should expect inverted logic.
If use_modulation is false, raw on/off timing will be produced without carrier.

functions.name: IRsend::begin
functions.description: Prepare the IR transmitter hardware and any internal timing for subsequent send operations.
requirements: Call begin() once after constructing IRsend and before any sending functions (e.g., enableIROut, mark/space/send...).

functions.name: IRsend::enableIROut
functions.signature: void IRsend::enableIROut(uint32_t freq, uint8_t duty = kDutyDefault)
functions.description: Configure the IR carrier frequency and duty cycle used when modulation is enabled. Typical carrier for many remotes is 38000 Hz.
requirements: freq should be a positive frequency in Hz (typical range ~30000–56000).
duty is a percentage (0–100) and should not exceed kDutyMax (100).
Call after begin() and before sending mark/space or protocol functions that rely on modulation.

functions.name: IRsend::_delayMicroseconds
functions.description: Internal/virtual microsecond delay helper used to accurately time IR marks and spaces.
requirements: usec is the delay duration in microseconds.
Accuracy of delayMicroseconds() is generally reliable up to kMaxAccurateUsecDelay (16383). Longer delays may be less accurate.

functions.name: IRsend::mark
functions.description: Generate a 'mark' period (IR LED on). If modulation is enabled, outputs carrier at the configured frequency and duty cycle for the specified duration.
requirements: Call enableIROut() to set frequency/duty if using modulation.
usec is the desired mark duration in microseconds; large values may accumulate timing error beyond kMaxAccurateUsecDelay.

functions.name: IRsend::space
functions.description: Generate a 'space' period (IR LED off) for the specified duration.
requirements: usec is the desired space duration in microseconds; accuracy beyond kMaxAccurateUsecDelay may be reduced.

functions.name: IRsend::calibrate
functions.description: Calibrate and compensate for software overhead when producing a PWM carrier at the given frequency. Returns an offset used to improve timing accuracy.
requirements: hz should be a typical carrier frequency (e.g., 38000).
Call after begin(); useful when precise protocol timings are required.

functions.name: IRsend::sendRaw
functions.signature: void IRsend::sendRaw(const uint16_t buf[], const uint16_t len, const uint16_t hz)
functions.description: Send a raw on/off sequence defined by alternating mark/space durations in microseconds. Uses the provided carrier frequency.
requirements: buf must be a non-null pointer to an array of length len containing durations in microseconds.
len must be the number of entries in buf; typically even (mark, space, ...), but pattern depends on usage.
hz is the carrier frequency used for marks; set to 0 or configure modulation appropriately if raw no-carrier is desired (behavior depends on implementation).
Call begin() before use.

functions.name: IRsend::sendData
functions.signature: void IRsend::sendData(uint16_t onemark, uint32_t onespace, uint16_t zeromark, uint32_t zerospace, uint64_t data, uint16_t nbits, bool MSBfirst = true)
functions.description: Pulse-distance (mark/space) data sender. Sends nbits from data using distinct mark/space pairs for logical 1 and 0.
requirements: Call begin() and enableIROut() prior to sending.
nbits must be between 1 and 64 inclusive.
Interpretation of bit order depends on MSBfirst (true means send most-significant bit first).
Timing parameters (onemark/onespace/zeromark/zerospace) are in microseconds and should match the target protocol.

functions.name: IRsend::sendManchesterData
functions.signature: void IRsend::sendManchesterData(const uint16_t half_period, const uint64_t data, const uint16_t nbits, const bool MSBfirst = true, const bool GEThomas = true)
functions.description: Send a Manchester-encoded bitstream (bi-phase). half_period controls the duration of each half-bit. GEThomas selects Thomas or G.E. encoding convention.
requirements: Call begin() and enableIROut() before use.
nbits must be between 1 and 64.
half_period is in microseconds and should match the target protocol's timing.
MSBfirst selects bit transmission order.
GEThomas chooses the Manchester phase convention (details protocol-specific).

functions.name: IRsend::sendManchester
functions.signature: void IRsend::sendManchester(const uint16_t headermark, const uint32_t headerspace, const uint16_t half_period, const uint16_t footermark, const uint32_t gap, const uint64_t data, const uint16_t nbits, const uint16_t frequency = 38, const bool MSBfirst = true, const uint16_t repeat = kNoRepeat, const uint8_t dutycycle = kDutyDefault, const bool GEThomas = true)
functions.description: Send a complete Manchester-framed message with header, payload, optional footer, and inter-message gap. Supports repeats, frequency, and duty cycle selection.
requirements: Call begin() before use.
frequency is in kHz or Hz depending on library convention; this header uses Hz elsewhere, so use Hz (e.g., 38000).
dutycycle is a percentage 0–100.
nbits must be 1–64.
Timing parameters are in microseconds.
repeat specifies additional transmissions after the first (protocol dependent).

functions.name: IRsend::sendGeneric
functions.signature: void IRsend::sendGeneric(const uint16_t headermark, const uint32_t headerspace, const uint16_t onemark, const uint32_t onespace, const uint16_t zeromark, const uint32_t zerospace, const uint16_t footermark, const uint32_t gap, const uint64_t data, const uint16_t nbits, const uint16_t frequency, const bool MSBfirst, const uint16_t repeat, const uint8_t dutycycle)
functions.description: Send a generic pulse-distance modulated message with explicit header/footer timings and a 0/1 definition. Payload is a 64-bit value.
requirements: Call begin() before use.
frequency is in Hz; dutycycle is 0–100%.
nbits must be 1–64.
All timing parameters are in microseconds and should match the target protocol.
MSBfirst controls bit order; repeat controls additional message sends.

functions.name: IRsend::sendGeneric
functions.signature: void IRsend::sendGeneric(const uint16_t headermark, const uint32_t headerspace, const uint16_t onemark, const uint32_t onespace, const uint16_t zeromark, const uint32_t zerospace, const uint16_t footermark, const uint32_t gap, const uint32_t mesgtime, const uint64_t data, const uint16_t nbits, const uint16_t frequency, const bool MSBfirst, const uint16_t repeat, const uint8_t dutycycle)
functions.description: Send a generic pulse-distance message like the other overload but enforces/uses a fixed total message time (mesgtime).
requirements: Call begin() before use.
mesgtime is in microseconds and should be consistent with the provided timings and nbits.
Other requirements are as per the 64-bit data overload.

functions.name: IRsend::sendGeneric
functions.signature: void IRsend::sendGeneric(const uint16_t headermark, const uint32_t headerspace, const uint16_t onemark, const uint32_t onespace, const uint16_t zeromark, const uint32_t zerospace, const uint16_t footermark, const uint32_t gap, const uint8_t *dataptr, const uint16_t nbytes, const uint16_t frequency, const bool MSBfirst, const uint16_t repeat, const uint8_t dutycycle)
functions.description: Send a generic pulse-distance message using a byte array payload rather than a 64-bit integer.
requirements: dataptr must be a non-null pointer to at least nbytes of data.
nbytes must reflect the payload length in bytes; bit order within bytes depends on MSBfirst.
Other timing/frequency/duty requirements are the same as the other overloads.

functions.name: IRsend::minRepeats

functions.name: IRAirtonAc::IRAirtonAc
functions.signature: IRAirtonAc::IRAirtonAc(const uint16_t pin, const bool inverted = false, const bool use_modulation = true)
functions.description: Constructor for an Airton 56-bit A/C IR controller. Creates an object bound to the given Arduino GPIO pin and configures signal polarity and modulation usage. Typically followed by begin() and then state configuration before send().
requirements: pin must be a valid GPIO capable of driving an IR LED via the IRsend backend on the target platform
begin() must be called before any send() or calibrate() usage to initialize hardware resources
inverted selects whether the output logic is inverted; choose according to your IR driver hardware
use_modulation should remain true for normal IR transmission at carrier frequency

functions.name: IRAirtonAc::stateReset
functions.description: Reset the internal Airton protocol state to library defaults (power/mode/fan/temp/flags). Used to start from a known configuration before making changes.
requirements: May alter all internal fields including mode, temperature, fan, and feature flags; callers should reapply desired settings after calling

functions.name: IRAirtonAc::send
functions.description: Transmit the current Airton 56-bit IR message, optionally repeating the frame a specified number of times. Available only when SEND_AIRTON is enabled.
requirements: Requires macro SEND_AIRTON to be enabled at build time
begin() must be called successfully before send() to initialize the IR transmitter
repeat is the number of extra transmissions and must be within 0..65535
The internal state should be configured to valid values (mode/fan/temp, etc.) before sending

functions.name: IRAirtonAc::calibrate
functions.description: Run IR transmitter timing calibration and return the microsecond per-modulation offset for this platform. Emits a ~65 ms 38 kHz IR burst. Only needs to be run once per object, if at all. Available only when SEND_AIRTON is enabled.
requirements: Requires macro SEND_AIRTON to be enabled at build time
Produces a visible IR output; ensure the IR LED is connected to the configured pin
Should be called after begin() so the transmitter is initialized

functions.name: IRAirtonAc::begin
functions.description: Initialize the underlying IR transmitter hardware for this instance. Must be called before send() or calibrate().
requirements: Must be called exactly once per object before any transmission or calibration
The configured pin must be available and not used by other peripherals

functions.name: IRAirtonAc::on
functions.description: Set the internal power state to ON. Equivalent to setPower(true). Does not transmit by itself until send() is called.
requirements: State change only; call send() to actually transmit the new state

functions.name: IRAirtonAc::off
functions.description: Set the internal power state to OFF. Equivalent to setPower(false). Does not transmit by itself until send() is called.
requirements: State change only; call send() to actually transmit the new state

functions.name: IRAirtonAc::setPower
functions.description: Set the internal power state flag to ON or OFF for the Airton message.
requirements: State change only; call send() to transmit
on is a boolean flag

functions.name: IRAirtonAc::getPower
functions.description: Return the current internal power state flag.

functions.name: IRAirtonAc::setTemp
functions.description: Set the target temperature in degrees Celsius for the Airton message. The protocol stores temp as value+16, and documented min/max are 16–31 C.
requirements: degrees must be within kAirtonMinTemp..kAirtonMaxTemp inclusive (16..31)
State change only; call send() to transmit

functions.name: IRAirtonAc::getTemp
functions.description: Get the current target temperature in degrees Celsius from the internal state.

functions.name: IRAirtonAc::setFan
functions.description: Set the fan speed field for the Airton message. Supported values are the Airton-specific constants (Auto/Min/Low/Med/High/Max).
requirements: speed should be one of: kAirtonFanAuto(0), kAirtonFanMin(1), kAirtonFanLow(2), kAirtonFanMed(3), kAirtonFanHigh(4), kAirtonFanMax(5)
State change only; call send() to transmit

functions.name: IRAirtonAc::getFan
functions.description: Get the current fan speed code from the internal state (Airton-specific numeric value).

functions.name: IRAirtonAc::setMode
functions.description: Set the operating mode for the Airton message using Airton mode codes (Auto, Cool, Dry, Fan, Heat).
requirements: mode should be one of: kAirtonAuto(0), kAirtonCool(1), kAirtonDry(2), kAirtonFan(3), kAirtonHeat(4)
State change only; call send() to transmit

functions.name: IRAirtonAc::getMode
functions.description: Get the current operating mode code from the internal state (Airton-specific numeric value).

functions.name: IRAirtonAc::getRaw
functions.description: Return the raw 64-bit value representing the 56-bit Airton protocol frame (including checksum byte).
requirements: Returned value encodes all fields; only lower 56 bits are meaningful for the Airton frame per union layout

functions.name: IRAirtonAc::setRaw
functions.description: Replace the internal state with a raw 64-bit Airton frame value. Useful for restoring or cloning a known frame.
requirements: data should represent a well-formed Airton 56-bit frame with fields as per AirtonProtocol and a correct checksum in the Sum byte; otherwise validation or device behavior may be undefined
After setting raw, callers may wish to validate with validChecksum(data)
State change only; call send() to transmit

functions.name: IRAmcorAc::stateReset

functions.name: IRAmcorAc::send
functions.description: Transmit the current Amcor A/C state via IR. Repeats the message repeat times as per protocol requirements. Only available when compiled with SEND_AMCOR.
requirements: Available only when the library is compiled with SEND_AMCOR defined.

functions.name: IRAmcorAc::begin
functions.description: Initializes the IR transmitter and prepares the IRAmcorAc instance for use. Typically called in setup() before any send() operations.

requirements: state must point to a readable buffer of at least length bytes.

functions.name: IRAmcorAc::validChecksum

requirements: state must point to a readable buffer of at least length bytes containing a complete Amcor message including checksum.

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::IRCarrierAc64
functions.signature: IRCarrierAc64::IRCarrierAc64(const uint16_t pin, const bool inverted = false, const bool use_modulation = true)
functions.description: Constructs a Carrier 64-bit A/C IR transmitter bound to a specific GPIO pin, with options for signal inversion and carrier modulation. Typical usage is to instantiate once, then call begin() and send() after configuring state.
requirements: pin must be a valid GPIO capable of driving an IR LED via the IRsend backend (per IRremoteESP8266/IRsend usage).
If inverted is true, the output logic level is inverted; choose according to your IR driver hardware.
If use_modulation is true, 38 kHz modulation is used; set false only if direct (unmodulated) drive is desired and supported by hardware.

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::stateReset
functions.description: Reset the internal CarrierProtocol state to library defaults for this protocol. Intended to put the object into a known baseline configuration before further adjustments.
requirements: Call before customizing settings if you need a known default state.
No arguments; affects only the internal stored state, not any device until send() is called.

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::send
functions.description: Transmit the currently configured Carrier 64-bit IR message, repeating it a specified number of times. Only compiled when SEND_CARRIER_AC64 is defined.
requirements: Requires that SEND_CARRIER_AC64 be defined at build time; otherwise this function is unavailable.
begin() should be called successfully before send() to initialize the IR transmitter hardware.
repeat controls the number of full message transmissions; valid range is library-dependent (kCarrierAc64MinRepeat or larger).
Hardware must be able to drive an IR LED at the configured pin.

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::calibrate
functions.description: Run IRsend timing calibration for this instance and return the microsecond offset per modulation period. Produces a ~65 ms 38 kHz IR pulse. Only compiled when SEND_CARRIER_AC64 is defined.
requirements: Requires that SEND_CARRIER_AC64 be defined at build time; otherwise this function is unavailable.
Emits a visible IR transmission during calibration (~65 ms at 38 kHz); ensure this won’t interfere with nearby devices.
Typically only needs to be run once per object instantiation, if at all.

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::begin
functions.description: Initialize the underlying IR transmitter (IRsend) for this instance. Must be called prior to sending IR messages.
requirements: Call once after constructing the object and before any call to send() or calibrate().
Pin hardware must be properly connected to an IR LED/driver compatible with IRsend.

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::calcChecksum
functions.description: Compute the 4-bit Carrier AC64 protocol checksum for the provided 64-bit state value. Intended for validating or constructing raw messages.
requirements: state must be a properly formatted Carrier AC64 64-bit frame; checksum is computed using kCarrierAc64ChecksumOffset and kCarrierAc64ChecksumSize semantics.
Returns only the checksum nibble; caller is responsible for inserting it into the message if needed.

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::validChecksum
functions.description: Check whether the provided 64-bit Carrier AC64 state has a valid checksum according to the protocol’s checksum definition.
requirements: state must represent a full Carrier AC64 64-bit frame including a checksum field at the defined offset.
Returns true if checksum matches, false otherwise; caller should handle false as an invalid/corrupt frame.

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::setPower
functions.description: Set the power flag in the stored Carrier AC64 state to turn the target A/C on or off on the next transmission.
requirements: on=true sets Power bit, on=false clears it; takes effect when send() is called.
Only affects internal state; does not change the physical device until transmission.

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::getPower
functions.description: Get the current power flag from the stored Carrier AC64 state.
requirements: Returns the internal state’s Power bit; may not reflect the actual device until a message is sent.

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::on
functions.description: Convenience method to set power on in the stored state.
requirements: Equivalent to setPower(true).
Does not transmit; call send() to apply to the device.

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::off
functions.description: Convenience method to set power off in the stored state.
requirements: Equivalent to setPower(false).
Does not transmit; call send() to apply to the device.

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::setTemp
functions.description: Set the target temperature (Celsius) in the stored state for the Carrier AC64 protocol.
requirements: Valid temperature range is 16–30 °C, per kCarrierAc64MinTemp and kCarrierAc64MaxTemp.
Values outside the supported range may be rejected or clamped by the implementation (exact behavior not specified here).
Takes effect on the device when send() is called.

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::getTemp
functions.description: Get the currently stored target temperature in Celsius from the internal state.
requirements: Returns the internal setting; may not reflect the actual device until a message is sent.

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::setSwingV
functions.description: Enable or disable vertical swing in the stored Carrier AC64 state.
requirements: on=true enables vertical swing; on=false disables it.
Effect is applied to the device upon send().

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::getSwingV
functions.description: Return the vertical swing setting from the stored state.
requirements: Reports only the internal state; actual device state may differ until transmission.

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::setSleep
functions.description: Enable or disable Sleep mode in the stored Carrier AC64 state.
requirements: on=true enables Sleep; on=false disables it.
Takes effect when the message is sent.

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::getSleep
functions.description: Get the Sleep mode flag from the stored state.
requirements: Reports the internal state only; transmit to apply.

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::setFan
functions.description: Set the fan speed in the stored state using Carrier AC64 fan codes.
requirements: speed should be one of: kCarrierAc64FanAuto (0), kCarrierAc64FanLow (1), kCarrierAc64FanMedium (2), or kCarrierAc64FanHigh (3).
Values outside 0–3 are invalid for this protocol.
Applies when send() is called.

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::getFan
functions.description: Get the fan speed code from the stored state.
requirements: Return value is a protocol code: 0=Auto, 1=Low, 2=Medium, 3=High.

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::setMode
functions.description: Set the operating mode in the stored Carrier AC64 state using protocol-specific codes.
requirements: Valid mode codes are defined constants: kCarrierAc64Heat (0b01), kCarrierAc64Cool (0b10), kCarrierAc64Fan (0b11).
The value 0b00 is not defined for this protocol in this header.
Applies to the device when send() is called.

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::getMode
functions.description: Get the operating mode code from the stored state.
requirements: Returned value is a raw protocol code; see setMode() accepted constants.

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::setOnTimer
functions.description: Configure the On Timer in the stored state, specifying a delay in minutes before powering on.
requirements: nr_of_mins is expressed in minutes.
Exact valid range/granularity is not fully specified here; constants indicate the device supports timers from 1 to 9 hours (kCarrierAc64TimerMin to kCarrierAc64TimerMax).
How to disable the On Timer is not specified in this header (unknown).
Takes effect when the message is sent.

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::getOnTimer
functions.description: Get the configured On Timer delay from the stored state, in minutes.
requirements: Returns minutes as stored internally; interpretation on the device may be in hour steps (exact behavior not specified here).

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::setOffTimer
functions.description: Configure the Off Timer in the stored state, specifying a delay in minutes before powering off.
requirements: nr_of_mins is expressed in minutes.
Exact valid range/granularity is not fully specified here; constants indicate the device supports timers from 1 to 9 hours (kCarrierAc64TimerMin to kCarrierAc64TimerMax).
How to disable the Off Timer is not specified in this header (unknown).
Takes effect when the message is sent.

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::getOffTimer
functions.description: Get the configured Off Timer delay from the stored state, in minutes.
requirements: Returns minutes as stored internally; interpretation on the device may be in hour steps (exact behavior not specified here).

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::getRaw
functions.description: Return the entire 64-bit Carrier AC64 message currently stored in the object, including all fields and checksum as maintained by the class.
requirements: The returned value represents the internal state; ensure checksum validity if using externally.
May recalculate or rely on previously calculated checksum (implementation detail not shown).

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::setRaw
functions.description: Replace the internal stored state with the provided 64-bit Carrier AC64 message.
requirements: state should be a correctly formatted Carrier AC64 frame. Use validChecksum(state) to verify before calling, or expect the class to update checksum later (not specified).
Caller is responsible for ensuring field values are valid for the protocol.

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::convertMode
functions.description: Convert a common stdAc operating mode to a Carrier AC64 raw mode code.
requirements: mode must be a valid stdAc::opmode_t value; unsupported mappings may map to a default or require caller handling (exact mapping not shown here).
Returned value is a protocol raw mode code suitable for setMode().

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::convertFan
functions.description: Convert a common stdAc fan speed to a Carrier AC64 raw fan speed code.
requirements: speed must be a valid stdAc::fanspeed_t value; unsupported mappings may map to nearest supported value (behavior not specified here).
Returned value is a protocol raw fan code suitable for setFan().

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::toCommonMode
functions.description: Convert a Carrier AC64 raw mode code to the corresponding stdAc common operating mode.
requirements: mode should be one of the protocol codes accepted by setMode().
Returns a stdAc::opmode_t; if the code is unrecognized, mapping behavior is unspecified in this header.

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::toCommonFanSpeed
functions.description: Convert a Carrier AC64 raw fan speed code to the corresponding stdAc common fan speed.
requirements: speed should be a value 0–3 per protocol constants.
Returns a stdAc::fanspeed_t; behavior for out-of-range codes is unspecified here.

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::toCommon
functions.description: Produce a stdAc::state_t representing the current stored Carrier AC64 state in common, brand-agnostic form.
requirements: Requires stdAc types to be available via included headers.
Conversion covers mode, fan, temperature, and applicable features supported by this protocol; exact field coverage is not detailed here.

functions.name: IRCarrierAc64::toString
functions.description: Return a human-readable summary of the current stored state as an Arduino String, suitable for debugging/logging.
requirements: Requires Arduino String type (not available on some non-Arduino builds unless provided).
Output format is implementation-defined and not specified here.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::IRCoolixAC
functions.signature: IRCoolixAC::IRCoolixAC(const uint16_t pin, const bool inverted = false, const bool use_modulation = true)
functions.description: Construct a Coolix A/C IR controller bound to a given transmit pin. Options allow electrical inversion and enabling/disabling 38 kHz modulation. Typically followed by begin() before sending.
requirements: pin must be a valid output-capable GPIO for the target platform (Arduino/ESP).
If the IR LED driver is inverting, pass inverted=true; otherwise leave default.
use_modulation should generally be true for IR; set false only if external hardware handles modulation.
Object should be constructed before any other member call.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::stateReset
functions.description: Reset the internal Coolix state to a known default (kCoolixDefaultState) and clear internal flags. Useful to start from a clean configuration.
requirements: Safe to call at any time to reinitialize the stored state.
Subsequent configuration (mode/temp/fan, etc.) may be needed before send().

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::send
functions.description: Transmit the current Coolix IR message using the IR LED. The frame is sent repeat times as required by the protocol.
requirements: Requires library compiled with SEND_COOLIX enabled.
begin() must be called successfully before send().
repeat should be a non-negative count; typical defaults are suitable for Coolix receivers.
Emits IR; ensure hardware IR LED/transistor is correctly connected to the configured pin.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::calibrate
functions.description: Run IR transmitter timing calibration and return the per-modulation microsecond offset. Produces a ~65 ms 38 kHz IR burst. Only needed once per object instantiation if at all.
requirements: Requires library compiled with SEND_COOLIX enabled.
Will actively transmit IR during calibration; ensure it’s safe to emit IR when calling.
Call after construction; begin() is not strictly required for calibration in IRsend, but typical usage calls begin() first. If unsure, call begin() before calibrate().

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::begin
functions.description: Initialize the underlying IR transmitter (pin modes, timers, etc.). Call before any send() operation.
requirements: Must be called once after construction and before send() or calibrate() in typical usage.
The configured pin must be available and not used by other peripherals.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::on
functions.description: Set the logical power state to ON in the internal Coolix message/state.
requirements: Affects only stored state until send() is called.
Mutually exclusive with off(); last call wins.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::off
functions.description: Set the logical power state to OFF in the internal Coolix message/state.
requirements: Affects only stored state until send() is called.
Mutually exclusive with on(); last call wins.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::setPower
functions.description: Explicitly set the logical power flag in the stored state.
requirements: Pass true to turn ON, false to turn OFF.
Only updates internal state; call send() to transmit.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::getPower
functions.description: Return the current logical power flag from the stored state.
requirements: None; query-only function.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::setTempFRange
functions.description: Enable Fahrenheit temperature mode for setTemp(), selecting the low (63–75F) or high (76–86F) mapping range. When high=true, use the upper Fahrenheit map; otherwise use the lower range.
requirements: Call clearTempFRange() to return to Celsius mode.
In F mode, setTemp() expects a Fahrenheit value within the selected range; values outside defined maps are invalid.
Exact interaction with current mode/fan is library-defined; behavior beyond selecting F maps is not documented.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::clearTempFRange
functions.description: Disable Fahrenheit mapping and revert setTemp() to Celsius range handling.
requirements: After clearing, setTemp() expects Celsius values in the Coolix range (17–30C).

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::setTemp
functions.description: Set the desired temperature in the stored state. Interprets temp in Celsius (17–30C) by default, or as Fahrenheit within the active F range if setTempFRange() was used.
requirements: In Celsius mode, temp must be in [17, 30] per kCoolixTempMin/Max.
If setTempFRange(false) was used, temp must be in [63, 75] F; if setTempFRange(true) was used, temp must be in [76, 86] F.
Values outside the active range are invalid/undefined.
Only updates internal state; call send() to apply on device.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::getTemp
functions.description: Get the currently stored setpoint temperature. Units reflect the current mode (Celsius by default; Fahrenheit if F range is active).
requirements: Returned units depend on whether Fahrenheit mapping is enabled.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::setSensorTemp
functions.description: Set the remote’s internal sensor temperature field in the Coolix message. Used by Zone Follow/Follow Me features in some remotes.
requirements: temp is in Celsius and should be within [0, 30] as kCoolixSensorTempMax=30; values above may be invalid.
Use clearSensorTemp() to indicate the sensor value should be ignored (sets ignore code).
Only updates internal state; call send() to transmit.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::getSensorTemp
functions.description: Get the stored sensor temperature value that will be encoded in the message.
requirements: If sensor temperature is set to the ignore code, returned value may reflect that encoded state rather than a physical temperature.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::clearSensorTemp
functions.description: Mark the sensor temperature field as ignored using the Coolix ignore code (0b11111).
requirements: Use when you don’t want to send a specific sensor temperature.
Only updates internal state; call send() to transmit.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::setFan
functions.signature: void IRCoolixAC::setFan(const uint8_t speed, const bool modecheck = true)
functions.description: Set the fan speed field in the stored state. Accepts Coolix fan codes (Min/Med/Max/Auto/etc.). modecheck optionally enforces mode constraints when setting the fan.
requirements: speed must be one of the defined fan codes: kCoolixFanMin (0b100), kCoolixFanMed (0b010), kCoolixFanMax (0b001), kCoolixFanAuto (0b101), kCoolixFanAuto0 (0b000), kCoolixFanZoneFollow (0b110), or kCoolixFanFixed (0b111), depending on device behavior.
If modecheck=true (default), fan changes may be restricted by the current mode (implementation-defined).
Only updates internal state; call send() to transmit.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::getFan
functions.description: Return the currently stored fan speed code.
requirements: Returned value is a Coolix fan code; translate via toCommonFanSpeed() for generic usage if needed.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::setMode
functions.description: Set the operating mode field (Cool/Dry/Auto/Heat/Fan) in the stored state.
requirements: mode must be one of: kCoolixCool (0b000), kCoolixDry (0b001), kCoolixAuto (0b010), kCoolixHeat (0b011), or kCoolixFan (0b100).
Only updates internal state; call send() to transmit.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::getMode
functions.description: Return the currently stored Coolix operation mode code.
requirements: Returned value is a Coolix mode code; convert with toCommonMode() if needed.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::setSwing
functions.description: Encode a Swing command/state in the stored Coolix message. Typically toggles or enables swing, depending on target A/C behavior.
requirements: Swing behavior can vary by model; this sets the state/command in the stored message.
Only updates internal state; call send() to issue the command.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::getSwing
functions.description: Return the stored logical Swing flag/state tracked by the library.
requirements: Represents the library’s notion of swing state; actual device state depends on prior transmissions.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::setSwingVStep
functions.description: Prepare a Vertical Swing Step command in the stored message (step the vertical louver).
requirements: Effect is typically a one-shot command; call send() to transmit.
Actual device behavior may vary by model.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::getSwingVStep
functions.description: Return whether a Vertical Swing Step is currently flagged in the stored state.
requirements: Represents internal flag only; may clear after handling depending on implementation (unknown).

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::setSleep
functions.description: Encode a Sleep command/state in the stored message.
requirements: Only updates internal state; call send() to transmit.
Sleep semantics are device-specific; library tracks a boolean flag.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::getSleep
functions.description: Return the stored logical Sleep flag.
requirements: Represents internal state; actual device behavior depends on transmitted commands.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::setTurbo
functions.description: Encode a Turbo (powerful) mode command/state in the stored message.
requirements: Only updates internal state; call send() to transmit.
Turbo semantics are device-specific; library tracks a boolean flag.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::getTurbo
functions.description: Return the stored logical Turbo flag.
requirements: Represents internal state; actual device behavior depends on transmitted commands.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::setLed
functions.description: Encode an LED (display backlight) toggle/command in the stored message.
requirements: Only updates internal state; call send() to transmit.
Exact effect (toggle vs. set) depends on device; the library tracks a boolean flag.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::getLed
functions.description: Return the stored logical LED flag.
requirements: Represents internal state tracked by the library.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::setClean
functions.description: Encode a Clean (self-cleaning/ion) command/state in the stored message.
requirements: Only updates internal state; call send() to transmit.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::getClean
functions.description: Return the stored logical Clean flag.
requirements: Represents internal state tracked by the library.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::getZoneFollow

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::getRaw

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::toCommonMode
functions.description: Convert a Coolix mode code to the common stdAc::opmode_t enumeration.

functions.name: IRCoolixAC::toCommonFanSpeed

functions.description: Construct an IRCoronaAc controller bound to a specific IR output pin. Provides high-level helpers to build and transmit Corona A/C IR messages via IRremoteESP8266. requirements: pin must be a valid GPIO capable of IR output on the target platform.

functions.name: IRCoronaAc::send

requirements: Requires SEND_CORONA_AC to be defined for this symbol to be available.
begin() should be called successfully before send() so the IR hardware is initialized (standard IRremoteESP8266 pattern).
repeat must be a non-negative count (kNoRepeat or greater).
The internal state should represent a valid Corona protocol message prior to calling (e.g., fields set via setters or setRaw()).

functions.name: IRCoronaAc::calibrate
functions.description: Run IR modulation timing calibration for the current platform and return the per-modulation microsecond timing offset. Produces a ~65 ms 38 kHz signal to measure timing. Only available when SEND_CORONA_AC is enabled.
requirements: Requires SEND_CORONA_AC to be defined for this symbol to be available.
An IR LED (or measurement setup) should be connected; calling may emit a 65 ms 38 kHz IR burst.
Should be run at most once per object instantiation unless environment changes.

functions.name: IRCoronaAc::begin
functions.description: Initialize the underlying IR transmitter (IRsend) for the configured pin and settings. Call before sending IR commands.
requirements: Must be called before send() to set up hardware pin modes and timers (per IRremoteESP8266 usage conventions).
Safe to call once after construction; repeated calls should be harmless but are unnecessary.
