functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::IRDelonghiAc
functions.signature: explicit IRDelonghiAc(const uint16_t pin, const bool inverted = false, const bool use_modulation = true)
functions.description: Constructor for the Delonghi A/C IR controller wrapper. Creates an IR sender bound to the given output pin, with optional signal inversion and carrier modulation control. Typical usage is to construct, call begin(), configure state (power, mode, temp, etc.), then send().
requirements: pin must be a valid Arduino GPIO capable of driving an IR LED (typically via a transistor).
begin() should be called once after construction before using send() or calibrate().
If inverted is true, output will be logic-inverted; set according to your driver circuit.
If use_modulation is true, a 38 kHz carrier is used; disable only if driving a demodulator directly or for testing.

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::stateReset
functions.description: Reset the internal DelonghiProtocol state to a known default for this device. Use to initialize or clear settings before applying new configuration.
requirements: Must be called on a valid IRDelonghiAc instance.
Subsequent setters (setMode, setTemp, etc.) should be used to configure after reset.

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::send
functions.description: Transmit the currently configured Delonghi A/C IR message, optionally repeating it a number of times as per protocol practice.
requirements: Available only when SEND_DELONGHI_AC is defined at compile time.
begin() must have been called successfully prior to send().
repeat is the number of extra transmissions; must be a non-negative integer value that fits in uint16_t.
The internal state should be valid (including checksum) before sending; use provided setters or setRaw() and checksum helpers.

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::calibrate
functions.description: Run IR timing calibration for this platform via the underlying IRsend. Returns the microsecond timing offset per modulation step. Produces a ~65 ms 38 kHz IR pulse train. Typically run once per object if needed.
requirements: Available only when SEND_DELONGHI_AC is defined at compile time.
begin() should be called before calibrate() so the sender is initialized.
This emits a visible IR burst; avoid calling continuously or during normal operation.

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::begin
functions.description: Initialize the underlying IR sender hardware for use (configure pin, timers, etc.). Call once after construction.
requirements: Must be called before send() and usually before calibrate().
The constructor pin must be a valid output-capable pin on the platform.

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::calcChecksum
functions.description: Compute the 8-bit checksum for a given 64-bit DelonghiProtocol state according to the Delonghi A/C message format (checksum byte at offset 56).
requirements: state must be a 64-bit value formatted per DelonghiProtocol.
Caller is responsible for inserting the returned checksum into the Sum field if mutating raw state.

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::validChecksum
functions.description: Validate that the checksum contained within a 64-bit DelonghiProtocol state matches the computed checksum.
requirements: state must be a 64-bit value formatted per DelonghiProtocol, with the checksum stored at byte offset 56.
Returns true only if the embedded checksum equals calcChecksum(state).

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::setPower
functions.description: Set the power flag in the Delonghi A/C state (turn the unit on or off in the next transmitted command).
requirements: on=true enables power; on=false disables power.
Call send() to transmit the updated state to the device.

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::getPower
functions.description: Get the current power flag from the stored Delonghi A/C state.
requirements: Returns the logical power state currently stored; does not query a physical device.

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::on
functions.description: Convenience method to set the power flag on.
requirements: Equivalent to setPower(true).
Call send() to transmit if desired.

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::off
functions.description: Convenience method to set the power flag off.
requirements: Equivalent to setPower(false).
Call send() to transmit if desired.

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::setTempUnit
functions.description: Set the temperature unit for subsequent temperature settings and reporting in the state. true selects Celsius; false selects Fahrenheit.
requirements: celsius=true selects Celsius; celsius=false selects Fahrenheit.
Changing units may affect valid temperature range for setTemp().

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::getTempUnit
functions.description: Return the currently configured temperature unit flag (true for Celsius, false for Fahrenheit).
requirements: Reports the unit tracked in the stored state; not a device query.

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::setTemp
functions.signature: void setTemp(const uint8_t temp, const bool fahrenheit = false, const bool force = false)
functions.description: Set the desired temperature in the stored state, with optional unit selection and forcing behavior. If fahrenheit is true, temp is interpreted in Fahrenheit; otherwise Celsius. The valid ranges are indicated by constants kDelonghiAcTempMinC/MaxC and kDelonghiAcTempMinF/MaxF. Special encodings exist for some modes (e.g., Auto/Dry/Fan).
requirements: If fahrenheit=false: temp should be within [kDelonghiAcTempMinC, kDelonghiAcTempMaxC].
If fahrenheit=true: temp should be within [kDelonghiAcTempMinF, kDelonghiAcTempMaxF].
Some modes may use special temperature field values (e.g., kDelonghiAcTempAutoDryMode, kDelonghiAcTempFanMode); caller should set mode appropriately when using such values.
force controls behavior when temp is outside normal bounds or mode constraints; exact effect is implementation-defined (unknown from header).

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::getTemp
functions.description: Get the current temperature value stored in the state (units depend on the configured temp unit or last setTemp call).
requirements: Returned value is the raw stored temperature code for the current unit context.

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::setFan
functions.description: Set the fan speed in the stored state. Supported codes are kDelonghiAcFanAuto, kDelonghiAcFanHigh, kDelonghiAcFanMedium, kDelonghiAcFanLow.
requirements: speed must be one of: kDelonghiAcFanAuto (0b00), kDelonghiAcFanHigh (0b01), kDelonghiAcFanMedium (0b10), kDelonghiAcFanLow (0b11).
Certain modes may constrain available fan speeds (not specified here).

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::getFan
functions.description: Get the current fan speed code from the stored state.
requirements: Returns a 2-bit code; compare against kDelonghiAcFan* constants.

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::setMode
functions.description: Set the operating mode in the stored state. Supported codes include kDelonghiAcCool, kDelonghiAcDry, kDelonghiAcFan, kDelonghiAcAuto.
requirements: mode should be a supported 3-bit code; use the kDelonghiAc* mode constants.
Mode may influence valid temperature or fan settings (caller should coordinate settings).

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::getMode
functions.description: Get the current operating mode code from the stored state.
requirements: Returns a 3-bit code; compare against kDelonghiAc* mode constants.

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::setBoost
functions.description: Enable or disable Boost (Turbo) mode in the stored state.
requirements: on=true enables Boost/Turbo; on=false disables it.
Some modes may not support Boost (not specified in header).

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::getBoost
functions.description: Return the current Boost (Turbo) flag from the stored state.
requirements: Reports stored flag; not a device query.

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::setSleep
functions.description: Enable or disable Sleep mode in the stored state.
requirements: on=true enables Sleep; on=false disables it.

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::getSleep
functions.description: Return the current Sleep flag from the stored state.
requirements: Reports stored flag; not a device query.

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::setOnTimerEnabled
functions.description: Enable or disable the power-on timer feature in the stored state.
requirements: on=true enables the On timer; on=false disables it.
When enabling, set the timer value via setOnTimer().

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::getOnTimerEnabled
functions.description: Return whether the power-on timer is enabled in the stored state.
requirements: Reports stored flag; not a device query.

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::setOnTimer
functions.description: Set the power-on timer delay in minutes in the stored state.
requirements: nr_of_mins must be within [0, kDelonghiAcTimerMax] minutes, where kDelonghiAcTimerMax == 23*60 + 59.
Enable the timer via setOnTimerEnabled(true) for it to take effect.

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::getOnTimer
functions.description: Get the current power-on timer value in minutes from the stored state.
requirements: Returned value is in minutes, within [0, kDelonghiAcTimerMax].

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::setOffTimerEnabled
functions.description: Enable or disable the power-off timer feature in the stored state.
requirements: on=true enables the Off timer; on=false disables it.
When enabling, set the timer value via setOffTimer().

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::getOffTimerEnabled
functions.description: Return whether the power-off timer is enabled in the stored state.
requirements: Reports stored flag; not a device query.

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::setOffTimer
functions.description: Set the power-off timer delay in minutes in the stored state.
requirements: nr_of_mins must be within [0, kDelonghiAcTimerMax] minutes, where kDelonghiAcTimerMax == 23*60 + 59.
Enable the timer via setOffTimerEnabled(true) for it to take effect.

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::getOffTimer
functions.description: Get the current power-off timer value in minutes from the stored state.
requirements: Returned value is in minutes, within [0, kDelonghiAcTimerMax].

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::getRaw
functions.description: Return the full 64-bit raw DelonghiProtocol state currently stored, including all fields (header, flags, timers, checksum, etc.).
requirements: Returned value reflects internal state; may be used with calcChecksum/validChecksum for validation.

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::setRaw
functions.description: Replace the internal state with a caller-provided 64-bit DelonghiProtocol value. Useful for importing a captured or prebuilt frame.
requirements: state must be a well-formed DelonghiProtocol frame matching the union layout, including fields such as Temp, Fan, Mode, timers, and checksum at offset 56.
Caller should ensure checksum correctness; use calcChecksum() and/or validChecksum() to prepare/verify.
Supplying malformed values can lead to undefined device behavior when sent.

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::convertMode
functions.description: Convert a common AC operating mode (stdAc::opmode_t) to the Delonghi protocol mode code (3-bit value).
requirements: mode must be a valid stdAc::opmode_t value supported by this mapping.
Returned value should be one of kDelonghiAcCool, kDelonghiAcDry, kDelonghiAcFan, kDelonghiAcAuto (or equivalent).

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::convertFan
functions.description: Convert a common AC fan speed (stdAc::fanspeed_t) to the Delonghi protocol fan code (2-bit value).
requirements: speed must be a valid stdAc::fanspeed_t value.
Returned value should be one of kDelonghiAcFanAuto/High/Medium/Low.

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::toCommonMode
functions.description: Convert a Delonghi protocol mode code to the common stdAc::opmode_t value.
requirements: mode must be a valid 3-bit protocol code; use kDelonghiAc* mode constants as reference.

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::toCommonFanSpeed
functions.description: Convert a Delonghi protocol fan speed code to the common stdAc::fanspeed_t value.
requirements: speed must be a valid 2-bit protocol code; use kDelonghiAcFan* constants as reference.

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::toCommon
functions.description: Translate the current stored Delonghi state into the library's common AC state representation (stdAc::state_t).
requirements: Depends on correct internal state; ensure settings are configured before calling.

functions.name: IRDelonghiAc::toString
functions.description: Return a human-readable summary of the current Delonghi A/C state as an Arduino String.
requirements: For diagnostics/logging; content and format are implementation-defined.

functions.name: IREcoclimAc::IREcoclimAc
functions.signature: explicit IREcoclimAc(const uint16_t pin, const bool inverted = false, const bool use_modulation = true)
functions.description: Constructs an EcoClim A/C IR transmitter/controller bound to a given output pin. Optional flags control output inversion and whether carrier modulation is used. Typically used with Arduino/IRremoteESP8266 to emit EcoClim 56‑bit messages.
requirements: pin must be a valid GPIO capable of driving an IR LED (directly or via a transistor), per platform/IRsend requirements
If inverted is true, the output logic is inverted (hardware must match)
If use_modulation is false, the IR carrier is not modulated; use only if the hardware/protocol expects unmodulated output
Call begin() before attempting to send() IR messages

functions.name: IREcoclimAc::stateReset
functions.description: Resets the internal EcoClim protocol state to a known default (kEcoclimDefaultState). Use to reinitialize the virtual remote to factory/default settings before further configuration.
requirements: No arguments; can be called at any time before send() to discard prior state

functions.name: IREcoclimAc::send
functions.description: Transmits the current EcoClim state as a 56‑bit IR message using IRremoteESP8266. The message may be repeated per the repeat count.
requirements: Available only when compiled with SEND_ECOCLIM enabled
begin() must be called successfully before send()
repeat must be a non‑negative integer; kNoRepeat (typically 0) sends once
Hardware must have an IR LED connected to the configured pin

functions.name: IREcoclimAc::calibrate
functions.description: Runs IR carrier timing calibration for the underlying IR transmitter and returns the per‑modulation timing offset in microseconds. Emits a ~65 ms 38 kHz IR pulse train during calibration. Typically run once after construction if precise timing is needed.
requirements: Available only when compiled with SEND_ECOCLIM enabled
Requires IR LED hardware connected; will actively transmit during calibration
Return value is an offset to be used internally by IRsend; callers should not assume other side effects

functions.name: IREcoclimAc::begin
functions.description: Initializes the underlying IR transmitter (IRsend) for use. Must be called before send().
requirements: Must be called once after constructing IREcoclimAc and before any send()
Safe to call multiple times; subsequent calls reinitialize the sender (behavior per IRsend)

functions.name: IREcoclimAc::on
functions.description: Convenience method to set the power state to ON in the internal EcoClim state.
requirements: Call send() after setting to actually transmit the change

functions.name: IREcoclimAc::off
functions.description: Convenience method to set the power state to OFF in the internal EcoClim state.
requirements: Call send() after setting to actually transmit the change

functions.name: IREcoclimAc::setPower
functions.description: Sets the power flag in the EcoClim state to ON or OFF.
requirements: Pass true to turn on, false to turn off
Call send() to transmit the updated state

functions.name: IREcoclimAc::getPower

functions.name: IREcoclimAc::setTemp
functions.description: Sets the desired target temperature (in Celsius) in the EcoClim state. Encoded on 5 bits per the protocol.
requirements: celsius should be within the protocol’s supported range: 5–36 °C (kEcoclimTempMin to kEcoclimTempMax)
Values outside the encodable range may be clamped or produce undefined behavior (not specified)
Call send() to transmit the updated state

functions.name: IREcoclimAc::getTemp
functions.description: Gets the desired target temperature (in Celsius) from the internal state.

functions.name: IREcoclimAc::setSensorTemp
functions.description: Sets the sensed/ambient temperature (in Celsius) field in the EcoClim state. Mainly used for state mirroring or testing; not all devices transmit or use this value.
requirements: celsius should be within 5–36 °C, inferred from 5‑bit temperature fields in the protocol
Call send() to transmit if desired

functions.name: IREcoclimAc::getSensorTemp
functions.description: Gets the sensed/ambient temperature (in Celsius) from the internal state.

functions.name: IREcoclimAc::setFan
functions.description: Sets the fan speed in the EcoClim state. Supported discrete speeds are per protocol constants.
requirements: speed should be one of: kEcoclimFanMin, kEcoclimFanMed, kEcoclimFanMax, or kEcoclimFanAuto
Call send() to transmit the updated state

functions.name: IREcoclimAc::getFan
functions.description: Returns the current fan speed setting from the internal state.

functions.name: IREcoclimAc::setMode
functions.description: Sets the operating mode in the EcoClim state (e.g., Auto, Cool, Dry, Fan, Heat, Recycle, Sleep) using protocol codes.
requirements: mode should be one of the kEcoclim* mode constants (e.g., kEcoclimAuto, kEcoclimCool, kEcoclimDry, kEcoclimRecycle, kEcoclimFan, kEcoclimHeat, kEcoclimSleep)
Call send() to transmit the updated state

functions.name: IREcoclimAc::getMode
functions.description: Gets the current operating mode from the internal state as the raw EcoClim mode code.

functions.name: IREcoclimAc::setClock
functions.description: Sets the internal clock field in the EcoClim state, expressed as minutes since midnight. The protocol allocates 11 bits for the clock.
requirements: nr_of_mins should be within a typical 24‑hour range 0–1439 minutes (inferred from usage and default state comment)
Values beyond the encodable range of 11 bits (0–2047) are invalid; behavior unspecified if exceeded
Call send() to transmit the updated state

functions.name: IREcoclimAc::getClock
functions.description: Gets the internal clock value in minutes from the EcoClim state.

functions.name: IREcoclimAc::getRaw
functions.description: Returns the raw 64‑bit EcoClim message/state as stored internally. Only the lower 56 bits are used by the protocol.
requirements: Callers should treat only the lower 56 bits as meaningful per EcoclimProtocol

functions.name: IREcoclimAc::setRaw
functions.description: Overwrites the internal state with the provided raw EcoClim message. Useful for importing a known IR code before transmission or analysis.
requirements: new_code should be a well‑formed EcoClim 56‑bit value; only the lower 56 bits are used
Caller is responsible for ensuring field consistency and validity when using raw codes
Call send() to transmit the updated state

functions.name: IREcoclimAc::setType
functions.description: Sets an internal type/variant code for the EcoClim A/C message/remote flavor. Exact semantics are not documented here.
requirements: code must be a valid type code recognized by this implementation (exact valid values unknown)

functions.name: IREcoclimAc::getType
functions.description: Returns the current internal type/variant code used by the encoder.

functions.name: IREcoclimAc::convertMode
functions.description: Converts a library‑standard AC operating mode (stdAc::opmode_t) to the corresponding EcoClim raw mode code for use with setMode().
requirements: mode must be a valid stdAc::opmode_t value
Returned value is an EcoClim mode code suitable for setMode()

functions.name: IREcoclimAc::convertFan
functions.description: Converts a library‑standard fan speed (stdAc::fanspeed_t) to the corresponding EcoClim raw fan code for use with setFan().
requirements: speed must be a valid stdAc::fanspeed_t value
Returned value is an EcoClim fan code suitable for setFan()

functions.name: IREcoclimAc::toCommonMode
functions.description: Converts an EcoClim raw mode code to the library’s common stdAc::opmode_t value.
requirements: mode should be a valid EcoClim mode code (e.g., kEcoclimAuto, kEcoclimCool, etc.)

functions.name: IREcoclimAc::toCommonFanSpeed
functions.description: Converts an EcoClim raw fan code to the library’s common stdAc::fanspeed_t value.

functions.name: IREcoclimAc::toCommon
functions.description: Converts the entire internal EcoClim state to the library’s common AC state representation (stdAc::state_t), including mode, temperature, fan, timers, and power.
requirements: Requires stdAc types to be available from IRremoteESP8266’s common AC API

functions.name: IREcoclimAc::setOnTimer

requirements: nr_of_mins must be encodable as (hours*60 + tens*10) with hours in 0–31 and tens in 0–7; maximum representable delay is 31*60 + 7*10 = 1930 minutes
To disable the ON timer, call disableOnTimer() or use kEcoclimTimerDisable (4774) if supported by implementation

requirements: nr_of_mins must be encodable as (hours*60 + tens*10) with hours in 0–31 and tens in 0–7; maximum representable delay is 1930 minutes

functions.name: IREuromAc::IREuromAc
functions.signature: explicit IREuromAc(const uint16_t pin, const bool inverted = false, const bool use_modulation = true);
functions.description: Construct an IR controller for Eurom A/C messages using the given output pin. Typical usage: instantiate once, call begin(), set desired state via setters, then send(). The inverted flag selects active-low output hardware. use_modulation selects whether to drive the IR LED at 38 kHz (normal) or as a raw/on-off signal.
requirements: pin must be a valid GPIO capable of IR transmission on the target platform (per IRsend requirements).
begin() should be called before attempting to transmit.
If inverted is true, the hardware output stage should expect inverted logic.
If use_modulation is false, carrier modulation is disabled; most IR LEDs/receivers expect 38 kHz so leave true unless hardware requires otherwise.

functions.name: IREuromAc::stateReset
functions.description: Reset the internal Eurom state to library defaults for this model (e.g., default mode, temperature, timers, and flags). Use when starting from a clean state before applying settings.
requirements: No arguments. Safe to call at any time before send().
Subsequent state reflects defaults; caller should reapply desired settings after calling.

functions.name: IREuromAc::send
functions.description: Transmit the current Eurom A/C state over IR. Optionally repeats the message repeat times as defined by the IRremoteESP8266 library.
requirements: This function is only available when compiled with SEND_EUROM enabled.
begin() should be called successfully before the first send().
repeat is a count of extra repeats; must fit in uint16_t. Use kNoRepeat for a single send.
An IR LED and suitable driver must be connected to the configured pin.
Calling may block briefly while transmitting.

functions.name: IREuromAc::calibrate
functions.description: Run IR carrier timing calibration for the current platform and return the per-modulation timing offset. Produces an approximately 65 ms IR burst at 38 kHz. Typically called once after construction if precise timing is needed.
requirements: This function is only available when compiled with SEND_EUROM enabled.
Emits a visible IR burst; ensure it will not interfere with nearby devices during calibration.
begin() is not required for calibration in IRsend, but hardware must allow toggling the output pin.

functions.name: IREuromAc::begin
functions.description: Initialize the IR transmitter backend for this instance. Call before send(). Safe to call once after construction.
requirements: Call exactly once before the first send() on this object.
Requires the configured GPIO to be available for output.

functions.name: IREuromAc::calcChecksum
functions.signature: static uint8_t calcChecksum(const uint8_t state[], const uint16_t length = kEuromStateLength);
functions.description: Compute the Eurom protocol checksum byte for a given raw state buffer using the protocol’s nibble-sum algorithm described in this header. Use to generate or verify the Checksum field for raw messages.
requirements: state must point to a buffer of at least length bytes containing a Eurom state.
length should typically be kEuromStateLength.
Does not modify the input buffer; returns the checksum byte to be stored in the protocol's checksum position.

functions.name: IREuromAc::validChecksum
functions.signature: static bool validChecksum(const uint8_t state[], const uint16_t length = kEuromStateLength);
functions.description: Validate the checksum of a Eurom protocol raw state buffer. Returns true if the buffer’s checksum byte matches the expected value.
requirements: state must point to a buffer of at least length bytes containing a full Eurom state including the checksum byte.
length should typically be kEuromStateLength.

functions.name: IREuromAc::setRaw
functions.description: Replace the internal device state with the provided raw Eurom protocol bytes. Useful when importing a captured state before sending or querying with getters.
requirements: state must point to a buffer of exactly kEuromStateLength bytes formatted per the Eurom protocol described in this header.
Caller is responsible for ensuring the provided state is coherent and has a correct checksum (see calcChecksum/validChecksum).
Supplying inconsistent combinations (e.g., unsupported mode/temperature pairs) may yield undefined device behavior.

functions.name: IREuromAc::getRaw
functions.description: Get a pointer to the mutable internal raw state buffer representing the Eurom message.
requirements: Returned pointer remains valid while the IREuromAc object exists and until setRaw/stateReset modifies it.
Modifying the buffer alters the object’s state; the caller must maintain protocol invariants and update the checksum field using calcChecksum to avoid invalid messages.
Do not hold the pointer across object destruction.

functions.name: IRGreeAC::IRGreeAC
functions.signature: IRGreeAC::IRGreeAC(const uint16_t pin, const gree_ac_remote_model_t model = gree_ac_remote_model_t::YAW1F, const bool inverted = false, const bool use_modulation = true)
functions.description: Construct a Gree A/C IR controller bound to a given transmitter pin and remote model. Use inverted and use_modulation to match the IR hardware/electronics. After construction, call begin() to initialize the IR sender before transmitting.
requirements: pin must be a valid GPIO capable of driving an IR LED via IRsend on the target platform
model must be a valid gree_ac_remote_model_t value; defaults to gree_ac_remote_model_t::YAW1F
If inverted is true, IR output levels will be inverted to suit hardware that inverts the signal

begin() should be called before send() to initialize the IR transmitter

begin() must have been called successfully prior to send()
repeat is the number of additional transmissions; must be a non-negative 16-bit value (typical range is small integers)
Hardware must have an IR LED connected to the configured pin

functions.name: IRGreeAC::calibrate
